correctness.rationale: Badziąg et al. establish the complete one-parameter pentagram spectrum. Trace alignment reduces every rank-two mixed state to a weighted sum of the two largest eigenvalues, and algebraic elimination gives the exact discriminant. Strict concavity and endpoint derivative signs prove the unique maximizer; the sign check makes the degree-six root unambiguous, including both endpoint cases. Exact symmetric-pentagon rays realize each spectral value and are independently verified. Symbolic reconstruction and numerical diagonalization pass, but finite checks are only auxiliary.

originality.rationale: Xu–Su–Chen (2015) specifically state that an analytic expression for rank-two curve AC is missing. 2009 Badziąg and 2012 Soeda et al. provide the pentagram spectrum and one-parameter optimization framework, which are explicitly credited and are NOT being claimed as new. The solved state-dependent sextic root with uniqueness and algebraic optimal measurements is absent from the inspected portions and not retrieved by focused search; the possibility of later unindexed implicit equivalents remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: The exact sextic-optimum solution could appear in an unindexed later paper or as an implicit specialization of a broad contextuality optimization result; search does not prove global novelty.
The one-parameter pentagram spectral polynomial, weighted expectation and general spectral reduction are definitively prior art, and must not be counted as novel.
The result only concerns rank-two qutrit states and does not classify all general full-rank qutrit KCBS optimizers.

value.rationale: The entire rank-two qutrit eigenvalue edge is a natural, physically motivated boundary, expressly identified as lacking an analytic expression in the 2015 study. The exact branch-selected sextic result classifies the global optimum for every state on this edge and algebraically constructs optimal measurements, replacing a central numerical boundary with a rigorous closed algorithm. The value is the solved complete natural classification, not a newly invented spectral invariant or tiny numerical improvement.
